spec_match.rationale: Probes the exact API surface (navigator.rtc and each of the three methods) and correctly lays out the three-layer enablement gate — [SecureContext], the RTCDiagnosticLogging flag/origin-trial exposure, and the WebRtcDiagnosticLogCollectionAllowedForOrigins enterprise policy — matching the chromestatus entry's enterprise framing.

interactive.rationale: A re-run button drives a live four-row presence table with per-surface detail, a live secure-context readout, and a status verdict distinguishing fully-present, partially-present, and absent; appropriate interactivity for a capability-gate concept.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises feature-detection of navigator.rtc and each method plus the full flag/origin-trial/enterprise-policy gate with no fake success; delivered exactly, including the honest no-public-trial-registration note.

edge_cases.rationale: Distinguishes absent binding, binding-present-but-method-missing, and insecure context, and the telemetry asserts probe-matches-reality consistency; the policy layer is honestly described as unobservable from the page.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5091582546149376 directly in the gate explanation, alongside both sibling concepts.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite's binding/method/secure-context assertions mirror this probe one-for-one; the 6 failures in this unflagged Chromium 141 are the expected absent surface the page itself reports as 'no'.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 CLI/CDP (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): the probe auto-ran — DOM shows all four rows honestly 'no', the secure-context tick, and the warn verdict pointing at step 2; zero console errors, no unintended failed requests; only the re-run button was not clicked.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts probe execution and the report-matches-reality consistency contract.

design_system.rationale: Tokenised colours and clean gate-step panels, but the default-visible warn status (--accent-amber on --bg-stone, ~3.5:1) and the flagged-path yes pill (--bg-ivory on --accent-emerald, ~4.0:1) sit under WCAG AA 4.5:1 at their small bold sizes.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled probe table with scoped headers, role=status aria-live verdict, and presence conveyed as yes/no text plus prose details rather than colour alone.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-emulated 360×740 DPR3 measures 0px horizontal overflow (cells use overflow-wrap:anywhere); desktop 1280×800 clean; only the environmental Google Fonts request fails.

openQuestions.title: Fix the shared amber/emerald sub-AA contrast
openQuestions.detail: The default-visible warn verdict (--accent-amber on --bg-stone, ~3.5:1) and pill.yes (--bg-ivory on --accent-emerald, ~4.0:1) miss AA 4.5:1 at their sizes — the same two tokens flagged across this milestone's critiques; one design-system-level darkening fixes every instance.

openQuestions.title: Record the fully-present probe on a flagged build and keep the origin-trial note fresh
openQuestions.detail: With --enable-blink-features=RTCDiagnosticLogging the table should flip to four yes rows and the ok verdict — capture that as evidence. The gate text also pins time-sensitive facts (OT desktop 150–155, no public registration as of 2026-07-24); re-check the ChromeStatus entry when the trial opens or the range shifts so step 2 stays accurate.

summary: A model capability-gate page for an enterprise-oriented API: honest per-method probing, a correct three-layer enablement story including the policy gate a page cannot observe, and dated origin-trial facts instead of vague framing. Verified with headless Chromium 141 via CLI/CDP (chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable in this environment): auto-run probe honestly all-no with the warn verdict, clean console, no unintended failed requests, no overflow on either device class. Open items: the shared amber/emerald contrast tokens and flagged-build all-yes evidence plus periodic refresh of the dated OT note.
